items.headline: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
items.blurb: Tens of thousands of people have been taking part in the strike, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.
items.text: Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living. Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas. The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant." There was a heavy police presence in the centre of Barcelona on Wednesday evening, with officers wearing helmets and riot shields. Some of the disturbances took place in the Passeig de Gràcia, close to the iconic Plaça de Catalunya in the centre of the city. items.headline: What could Chinese intelligence have learned from Nvidia CEO’s affair?
items.blurb: Nvidia says no secrets were compromised, but experts question what sensitive information may have been exposed.
items.text: United States lawmakers are pushing for answers from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid growing concerns over whether an affair he had compromised national security. Huang, 63, has admitted to having extramarital relations during his time leading Nvidia, a major US tech firm. Media reports indicate the woman involved was Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based tech company Megaspeed who is accused of working for Chinese intelligence. As the scandal continues to grip Washington, Republican leaders of three committees in the House of Representatives have asked Huang to appear at a closed-door briefing to testify about the relationship. House Foreign Affairs Committee Chair Brian Mast said he was prepared to subpoena Huang if he did not respond by the end of Wednesday. According to The New York Times, US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese intelligence to gather information about the Nvidia CEO and influence him to push for looser restrictions on chip sales to China. items.text: Seven-time F1 world champion tours border area and logistics warehouses operated by Egyptian Red Crescent Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory. The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire. “I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine . I think there’s a lot of peace that I’m hoping we get to at some stage,” Hamilton said in October. A ceasefire agreement reached last year has halted major combat operations in Gaza, but the amount of aid reaching the territory continues to fall far short of the agreed-upon minimum of 600 trucks a day. items.headline: Democrat Scott Colom seals historic win in Mississippi Senate race
items.blurb: Colom is the first black person from the southern state elected to the US Senate in over 140 years.
items.text: Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades. Colom's victory makes him the first black person from Mississippi to be elected to the US Senate in more than 140 years. Only a few thousand votes separated him from his Republican opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. The result means the Democrats will hold 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with a knife-edge race in Alaska still to be called. Colom won with 49.2% of the vote, while Hyde-Smith received 48.7% and an independent candidate got 2.1%, according to figures from CBS. Hyde-Smith congratulated Colom in a video posted on X on Wednesday evening and wished him well. "While this was not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said. items.headline: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
items.blurb: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
items.text: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said. The health ministry gave the casualty toll, adding more than 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment. Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years the government has announced modernisation initiatives to improve its railways. items.headline: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough
items.blurb: Talks in Abu Dhabi centred around Europe's security framework, with US envoys due to meet Putin and Zelensky on Thursday.
items.text: Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have concluded after a second day. Although the American side said they saw "some openings", there was no hint of any breakthroughs to end the nearly five year-long war sparked by Russia's invasion. However, both Moscow and Kyiv confirmed that a large-scale prisoner of war exchange was in the works and could be carried out soon. Davyd Arakhamia from Ukraine's negotiating team said that this round of talks - the first since February - "was one of the hardest." "I believe the Russians came with very strict directives, so it was extremely difficult to soften the discussion," he said. But he added that he felt "good momentum" and urged for a second round of talks to be organised as soon as possible. Comments by Kremlin negotiator Vladimir Medinsky were less conciliatory. items.headline: Former Italian Red Brigades member escapes house arrest in Argentina
items.blurb: Bertulazzi used a rope and harness to climb down from a fifth-floor apartment and evade authorities in Argentina.
items.text: A 74-year-old former member of Italy’s far-left Red Brigades has escaped from house arrest in Argentina by climbing down from a fifth-floor apartment using a harness and rope, prompting a nationwide search. Leonardo Bertulazzi, who faces extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence, escaped on Tuesday and was still on the run on Wednesday, Argentine police officials told The Associated Press news agency. Bertulazzi was convicted in absentia by a court in his home country for his role in the kidnapping and death of a former Italian prime minister by the left-wing armed group, and his refugee status in Argentina was revoked under right-wing President Javier Milei. Police said he descended onto the second-floor terrace of a neighbouring house, climbed down to a first-floor terrace, crossed a vacant lot and got onto the street by climbing over a gate. Authorities did not immediately notice Bertulazzi was gone as he had tampered with his electronic ankle monitor, the officials said. items.text: See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester . See My World , a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November. The festival is part of See My World’s year-round programme showcasing pan-African arts, culture and events. It reflects the determination among creatives and activists in Manchester to build on the legacy of the 1945 Pan-African Congress in Manchester – which connected luminaries of postwar independence movements with a shared vision of liberation – after last year’s 80th anniversary commemorations . items.headline: Stand-Up India and Mudra Yojana extended by Union Cabinet for 5 more years
items.blurb: The Union Cabinet allocated ₹4,111 crore for the Stand-Up India fund and ₹5,000 crore for the Micro Units fund under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana.
items.text: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved the continuation of two credit guarantee schemes for five years, allocating ₹ 4,111 crore for the Stand-Up India fund and ₹ 5,000 crore for the Micro Units fund under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), aimed at expanding collateral-free credit to women, SC/ST and micro entrepreneurs, according to an official release. According to the government, the Credit Guarantee Fund for Stand-Up India will guarantee loans above ₹ 10 lakh and up to ₹ 1 crore for women and SC/ST entrepreneurs setting up greenfield enterprises. The scheme targets an average of two loans per bank branch—one to a woman entrepreneur and one to an SC/ST entrepreneur. The guarantee fee will be 0.50% annually, with no additional risk premium, while the guarantee cover will be increased to 85% across loan sizes. Borrowers will also receive support through the loan process and business cycle. Meanwhile, the PMMY Credit Guarantee Fund is expected to support Mudra loans worth ₹ 12.60 lakh crore. items.headline: Rights panel steps in to address alleged contamination of well water near temple
items.blurb: The PCB and temple committee have assured that water contamination near the temple will be permanently resolved once the new waste treatment plant becomes operational
items.text: Inspections revealed several violations, including inadequate dust-control measures, improper storage and disposal of construction waste, and excessive noise levels. | Photo Credit: RAMAKRISHNA G A solution appears to be in sight to the alleged contamination of well water near the Thiruvarinikkulam Devi Temple during the 10-day-long Nadathurappu festival, attended by thousands each year, thanks to the intervention of State Human Rights Commission Chairperson Alexander Thomas. The State Pollution Control Board (PCB) and the temple committee office-bearers assured the Commission that the issue of water contamination would be permanently resolved once the new waste treatment plant at the temple becomes operational. The Commission directed the Sreemoolanagaram panchayat secretary to submit a report after testing a sample of well water from the temple’s neighbourhood once the treatment plant becomes operational. The directive was issued on a petition filed by Sujikumar, a resident living around 300 metres from the temple entrance, alleging that the water in his well became polluted during the temple festival. items.headline: Hoax note on Air India Kolkata-Mumbai flight sparks hijack scare
items.blurb: The note was found by the cabin crew of flight AI 2772, an Airbus A320 (VT-TNH), at around 10.37am, when it was scheduled to depart.
items.text: A hijack threat to an Air India flight from Kolkata to Mumbai triggered a security scare at the Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport in Kolkata on Wednesday after a handwritten warning was found in the aircraft’s lavatory before take-off, prompting security agencies to carry out mandatory checks, officials aware of the matter said. The note was found by the cabin crew of flight AI 2772, an Airbus A320 (VT-TNH), at around 10.37am, when it was scheduled to depart. It warned that the aircraft would be hijacked at 11.10am, officials said. The Air Traffic Control (ATC) was immediately informed, after which all concerned agencies swung into action, they said. “The aircraft was moved to an isolation bay and the mandatory security drill was initiated,” an airport official requesting anonymity said. All 105 passengers and seven crew members were deboarded and security personnel thoroughly searched the aircraft to rule out any potential threat “as per established protocols,” the official quoted above said. items.headline: Two SPOs go missing in J&K's Kishtwar; massive search operation launched
items.blurb: The officials said the two SPOs were travelling from Kiyar camp to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah when they failed to reach their destination
items.text: Two Special Police Officers (SPOs) went missing from the higher reaches of Dachhan in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district on Wednesday (November 12, 2026), prompting security forces to launch a massive joint search operation to trace them, officials said. The missing personnel have been identified as Babi Chand (57) and Rashpal Kumar (45), both of whom were posted with the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the local police at their Kiyar village in Dachhan, the officials said. They said the two SPOs were travelling from Kiyar camp to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah when they failed to reach their destination. Their mobile phones were initially reachable but were later switched off, raising concerns about their whereabouts. Following their disappearance, a massive search operation was launched jointly by the police and the Army's Rashtriya Rifles to locate the missing personnel. Security teams were deployed in the surrounding areas, including difficult and mountainous forest terrain, to establish their whereabouts and ascertain the circumstances surrounding their disappearance, the officials said. items.headline: ‘You will know at the right time’: Sunetra Pawar amid buzz on merger of NCP factions
items.blurb: Maharashtra deputy CM Sunetra Pawar addressed reporters in Baramati on Wednesday during preparations for Birsa Munda's birth anniversary celebrations.
items.text: Amid fresh speculations about a merger between the Sunetra Pawar -led Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) and the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP), NCP national president and deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar commented on the matter for the first time on Wednesday, saying the details would be revealed at an appropriate time. Responding to a question about the possibility of the two NCP factions coming together, Pawar told reporters in Baramati, “I know you people are more interested in the other issue. Despite that, I would like to tell you that you will come to understand things when the time comes.” The deputy chief minister was addressing a press conference regarding programmes being organised by the state government to mark the 191st birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda on November 15. The question about the merger was posed soon after she opened the forum and the media interaction was called off immediately after she responded to it. The NCP president’s statement came hours after the party’s chief spokesperson Umesh Patil told reporters, “No discussions are currently underway on the merger.”

items.text: The board of Nvidia, the second-most valuable company in the world, is preparing to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang after US media reports claimed that he was involved in an extramarital affair with a senior executive who reported to him. The New York Times on Wednesday reported that Huang had an affair with Nvidia's vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. According to the NYT, Huang and Powell were reportedly captured on camera being affectionate with one another at a hotel in San Jose, California, in March. The bombshell allegation comes at a time when the Nvidia board was already conducting an independent investigation into the 63-year-old after he, in an email to employees, admitted to infidelity. US intelligence believes that the Chinese executive, Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, with whom the Nvidia CEO had the affair, was a Chinese spy . items.blurb: Is HDFC Bank's recent underperformance a rare buying opportunity or a warning sign? A look at the key forces shaping its next big move.
items.text: HDFC Bank is one of the most recognised and respected names in corporate India. It’s the largest private sector bank in India by assets, and among the largest banks in the world by market capitalisation. After its merger with HDFC Ltd in 2023, the combined entity became the world's seventh-most valuable bank, with about 120 million customers and more than 177,000 employees. As of 30 September 2026, it had 9,706 branches and 20,881 ATMs in 4,177 cities and towns, as well as 14,365 business correspondents. The bank is heavily focused on technology and digital banking, including internet banking, phone banking, and mobile banking. Management’s main focus areas are retail banking, high-net-worth individuals, large corporations, public sector entities, as well as micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). HDFC Bank stock has underperformed the Nifty 50 over the past year amid concerns of a growth slowdown and pressure on its net interest margin (NIM). items.headline: Some under-25s should get less benefits, Milburn review to say
items.blurb: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.
items.text: Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to, under a radical overhaul of the system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review. Alan Milburn's year-long report, which will be published on Tuesday, will recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits, the Times reported , external . Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 18- to 24-year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet". He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants. His report is expected to recommend that under-25s are no longer able to claim the health element of universal credit or personal independence payment (Pip). Instead, they would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit. items.blurb: Khaitan & Co., Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas, Trilegal, and JSA Advocates and Solicitors expand partner ranks by up to 20% in FY27.
items.text: India's law firms are expanding their partner ranks through a mix of promotions and hires, with top players such as Khaitan & Co, Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas (CAM), Trilegal, JSA Advocates and Solicitors, and Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas (SAM) reporting a 6–20% year-on-year increase in the number of partners across taxation, real estate, disputes, financing and capital markets divisions. The increase in the industry's overall partner count has gone through crests and troughs. Ankita Malik, senior consultant at Vahura, a legal consulting firm, said expansion at several law firms was constrained during the pandemic but then the overall partner count rose 14% in FY25 amid robust business growth. The growth eased to 10% in FY26, she said. Mushrooming of niche and boutique legal firms has now ushered in a war for talent , which is likely to raise the partner-level hirings and promotions of the overall sector to about 12% in FY27, Malik said. items.text: Unacademy co-founder and CEO Gaurav Munjal is moving to the role of Executive Chairman, with chief business officer (CBO) Akhilendra Kumar set to take over as the company's new chief executive. Announcing the leadership transition in a post on X, Munjal said he would remain actively involved in the company's day-to-day operations and work alongside Kumar. He also said he would help with the upGrad IPO. Kumar is currently the CBO at Unacademy and has been with the company for nearly five years. The leadership change comes nearly two months after upGrad completed its acquisition of Unacademy in September 2026 in an all-stock deal valued at just over $200 million. The transaction marked a steep decline from Unacademy's peak valuation of around $3.4 billion in 2021. The acquisition gives upGrad an entry into the online test preparation segment, including UPSC, JEE, NEET and GATE, while adding Unacademy's educator network to its existing higher education, upskilling and study abroad businesses. items.blurb: Pune-based renewable fuels startup Greenjoules has raised Rs 150 crore in a Series B funding round co-led by Amazon’s Smbhav Venture Fund and Climate Pledge Fund. The round also saw participation from Rainmatter, the investment arm of Zerodha, and Singularity’s Strategic Autonomy Fund.
items.text: Pune-based renewable fuels startup Greenjoules has raised Rs 150 crore in a Series B funding round co-led by Amazon’s Smbhav Venture Fund and Climate Pledge Fund. The round also saw participation from Rainmatter, the investment arm of Zerodha, and Singularity’s Strategic Autonomy Fund. Blue Ashva Capital, which led the company’s Series A round in 2021, remains its largest shareholder. Separately, Greenjoules has secured a Rs 100 crore loan from the Technology Development Board (TDB), under the Department of Science and Technology. The combined Rs 250 crore financing will support the company’s expansion plans. The proceeds will be deployed to set up a manufacturing facility at Khed City in Pune, with a planned capacity to produce 200,000 litres of biocrude per day from agricultural waste. The facility will be developed in phases, starting in 2027, Greenjoules said in a press release. Founded in 2018 by S. Viraraghavan, Radhika Viraraghavan, Shweta Viraraghavan and Sethunath Ramaswamy, Greenjoules converts agricultural and agro-industrial waste into renewable fuels using its proprietary Integrated Catalytic Thermocracking (ICTC) technology. Its biocrude is further processed into renewable diesel and bio-naphtha.

items.blurb: Any amount of AI coding is too much for many Independent Games Festival judges.
items.text: The last few years have seen significant debate over the widespread use of AI-powered tools in game development and the responsible disclosure of that usage to players. That debate has exploded into a full-blown controversy in the indie game development space this week, as Big Walk developer House House has publicly and belatedly disclosed minimal AI use in its popular co-operative puzzle exploration game. This particular controversy has been brewing behind the scenes for months, as judges and jury members for the prestigious Independent Games Festival Awards discussed the issue in private discussion groups. items.headline: Google DeepMind just mathematically verified key parts of Signal
items.blurb: The four-week project hints that AI could make formal verification far more practical.
items.text: Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or “formally verify,” a number of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees—a landmark development for the widely used cryptography and AI itself. More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn’t have critical vulnerabilities. Before the AI era, it was incredibly time-consuming for people to describe the characteristics of software they wanted to prove, turn these summaries into formulas, and then develop the proof. Agentic AI can significantly cut down the time of the latter project, enabling analyses like DeepMind’s Signal evaluation. For specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol, digital transformation is all about giving researchers the tools to test ideas faster, make better-informed decisions, and develop more sustainable materials without compromising performance. Girish Rao, vice president of information technology at Lubrizol, says the company is building a digital foundation that connects business processes, modern data platforms, and cloud infrastructure to support its research and development (R&D) teams. Their goal is to combine decades of accumulated technical data with the deep expertise of chemists and engineers who understand customer needs as well as the physical constraints of their work. Data scientists can help identify patterns, test new hypotheses, and model possibilities before researchers conduct physical experiments. DeepMind’s new DNA model better predicts how mutations affect different cells, potentially opening paths to treatment. Researchers at Google DeepMind have unveiled a new AI model designed to unravel how changes in our DNA affect different cells, giving scientists a more detailed view of a notoriously difficult problem that could hold important clues to the causes of disease — and point the way to new treatments. AlphaGenome 2 is the successor to DeepMind’s genome-predicting AI model AlphaGenome, which was released last year . While nearly every cell in the human body carries the same DNA, different types of cells — from heart muscle cells and skin cells to immune cells fighting an infection — switch different genes on and off, and those patterns can change depending on what a cell is doing. In order to ensure an authentic experience, I didn’t tell Tau Robotics, the startup behind the X post, that I was a journalist—though I did use my real name, so it’s possible someone looked me up. items.blurb: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where…
items.text: As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where the backlash now sweeping the country arguably first began taking shape. Driving through it is surreal. Concrete monolithic buildings loom along every major road, with names like Skybox and CloudHQ. It’s accepted wisdom in Big Tech that the war against data centers must be about something bigger than just data centers themselves. Two days after the midterms, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, wrote that data centers “have become a proxy for public unease about affordability, corporate power, and people losing control over their futures.” It’s a culture war, in other words. But spending a few days in Data Center Alley left me wondering if it’s really the proxy that Lehane describes. I came away convinced that the data center backlash is more about electricity than Big Tech admits. See our ethics statement. United says it won’t let personal AI assistants book tickets on the airline, citing both privacy and regulatory concerns. The company says it hasn’t yet seen many people try to use AI agents to book their flights, The Wall Street Journal reports , in line with observations from other businesses like Doordash . But United is concerned that agents could expose customers’ information or make purchases they didn’t intend, and potentially skirt federal rules about the kind of information airlines need to share with customers — like having them attest that their bags don’t have explosives. While agents can still show users United flights, they won’t be able to actually complete the transaction on their behalf. The decision, and others like it, could limit the potential usefulness of newer personal AI assistants like Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots .

items.text: Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech's largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position. Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat against Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor against the Republican incumbent, Greg Abbott. At the state level, Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. Talarico and Hinojosa made data centers a central issue, discussing them constantly on the campaign trail. items.text: The race to build smarter AI models is giving way to AI inference: Running them efficiently at scale. Indian startups are stepping in. Nations worldwide have spent the last few years obsessing over bigger models and the compute power needed to train them. However, as models move into everyday products, it is becoming difficult to run AI models faster, cheaper and reliably at scale. This is where inference platforms are emerging as saviours. Now, before we dive into the topic, let’s first understand what inference actually means. Simply put, inference is the process through which a trained AI model uses what it has learned to respond to new inputs, such as questions, images or instructions. For context, when you ask an AI model to summarise a health report or a business document, it uses its existing capabilities to process your request and generate a response. items.headline: NVIDIA Scandal & AI Selloff In the US: India’s Neocloud Boom Faces Twin Tests
items.blurb: The alleged espionage scandal involving NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and the growing scrutiny of the chipmaker’s business dealings with China…
items.text: A selloff in US-listed neoclouds and growing scrutiny of NVIDIA have raised questions about the financing model underpinning the AI infrastructure boom, with potential implications for India's GPU cloud providers. Unlike their US peers, backed by large hyperscaler customers, Indian neoclouds have only limited domestic anchor demand and rely on international customers, government-backed compute requirements and evolving financing arrangements to fund expansion. As NVIDIA’s influence extends beyond GPU supply to financing and strategic partnerships, Indian players face questions around debt exposure, customer commitments, GPU depreciation and whether their infrastructure investments can withstand a global market correction. The alleged espionage scandal involving NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and the growing scrutiny of the chipmaker’s business dealings with China have added another layer of uncertainty to the global AI infrastructure market already facing questions about its financing model.
